body.statement: Uniformly over \(\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}(\alpha,\beta,L,c,\varepsilon)\), the deterministic lower-envelope quotas and the interval \(I_{T,\Delta}\) are uniformly honest and have expected length at most a constant multiple of \(r_{T,\Delta}\).
body.justification: This separates the one-sided condition needed for a policy-uniform upper bound from the two-sided comparability regime needed to identify an exact minimax sampling frontier.
body.gap: Shi, Wang, and Wu use one-sided forced exploration for delayed asymptotic inference under outcome-delay independence; the proposition isolates what survives under unrestricted outcome-delay dependence without attributing the new two-sided regime to them.
body.consumer: Analysts whose logs certify only a forced-exploration floor can retain the honest construction while reporting an upper guarantee rather than an exact policy-class minimax rate.
body.proof_tex:
The already established one-sided minimax-length theorem applies to exactly \(\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}(\alpha,\beta,L,c,\varepsilon)\) and to the same deterministic quotas and interval. Its first two displays state respectively
\[
 \inf_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}}
 P\{\tau\in I_{T,\Delta}\}\geq1-\eta-o(1)
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}}
 E_{P,\Pi}|I_{T,\Delta}|\leq C_\eta r_{T,\Delta}.
\]
These are precisely the two assertions of the corrected proposition. In particular, its achievability conclusion uses the arm-one lower allocation envelope and the control floor through the deterministic quota orders; no upper allocation envelope is used.
